explanation: Repeatedly clear the lowest set bit with n AND (n minus one). Count the iterations; the input represents an unsigned 32-bit bit pattern in a long. JavaScript normalizes each bitwise result with >>>0 so a set high bit remains an unsigned nonnegative pattern.
timeComplexity: O(b) time for b set bits, at most 32 iterations. Each iteration removes one set bit, and an unsigned 32-bit value contains at most 32.
spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space. Only the input accumulator and count are retained.
attribution: Original repository-authored Blind75 JavaScript algorithm, promoted from the validated correct fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: Each operation n & (n-1) clears exactly the lowest set bit without changing any other set bit. Counting such operations until n becomes zero therefore counts all ones in the original unsigned 32-bit pattern.
walkthrough: For n=21, the bits are 10101. Successive clears give 10100,10000,0. Three bits were removed, so return 3.
edgeCases: The input is an unsigned 32-bit value carried in a long.
A pattern with all 32 bits set returns 32.
